standards.name: Data required for the assignation of Digital Object Identifiers in the Global Information System (GLIS descriptors) v2.1
standards.abstract: This standard defines the metadata descriptors required when registering Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (PGRFA) in the Global Information System (GLIS) through the DOI assignment service. The research objects are PGRFA samples (genebank accessions, breeding lines, in situ materials, seed lots, etc.), documented to enable unique, permanent identification (DOIs) and interoperability across information systems. Published and maintained by the Secretariat of the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA) / FAO, the document (v2.1, 20 July 2017) groups descriptors into mandatory, highly recommended and additional/context-dependent classes, and supplies explicit named descriptors (e.g. M01–M04) with selectable forms and controlled choices. Its scope is metadata required for DOI assignation and discovery in GLIS (not the technical formatting rules, which are provided separately); it builds on survey results and advisory committee recommendations and aims to facilitate interoperability and reduce registrant burden by harvesting data from existing systems where possible.

classification.rationale: The source document is a formal list of named descriptors (M01, M02, M03, M04, etc.) each defined as a discrete metadata field with prescribed forms or allowable values (e.g. code, PID, date, enumerated method choices). The document provides field-level structure (explicit field names, short codes like [ACQDATE], options and constraints), therefore it is a genuine Metadata Table rather than prose guidance or a process DAG.

M01.name: Organization/individual conserving the PGRFA
M01.descr: Specify the organization, individual or legal entity conserving the PGRFA by selecting the first applicable form among the following: FAO-WIEWS Institute code; Your PID from Easy-SMTA; Organization name and address; Individual name and address.
possible_values: Organization name and address (string / structured address)
Individual name and address (string / structured address)
M01.evidence:
M01. Organization/individual conserving the PGRFA
Specify the organization, individual or legal entity conserving the PGRFA by selecting the
first applicable form among the following:
1 FAO-WIEWS Institute code1 (use this if you are acting for an organization and your
organization is registered in WIEWS) [INSTCODE]2
2 Your PID from Easy-SMTA (use this if you have a PID but not a FAO-WIEWS Institute code)
3 Organization name and address (use this if you are acting for an organization and your
organization does not have a FAO-WIEWS Institute code or a PID). For in situ material this
may be the protected area authority, or the owner of the area where material is conserved.
4 Individual name and address (use this if you are acting as an individual in your own right
and you do not have a PID)

M02.name: PGRFA unique identifier
M02.descr: The identifier used by the holder to identify the PGRFA material and distinguish it from other PGRFA they conserve. Specify precisely one identifier for the material; it must be unique among the PGRFA conserved by the holder.
M02.evidence:
M02. PGRFA unique identifier
The identifier that you use to identify your PGRFA material to distinguish it from other
PGRFA conserved by you. Specify precisely one identifier for the material. Make sure that it
is unique among the PGRFA conserved by you, and sufficient to enable you to identify the
PGRFA when you see this identifier, for example if a future GLIS user contacts you or your
successor about it.

M03.name: Date [ACQDATE]
M03.descr: Date on which you became the holder of the PGRFA. Date fragments are accepted (e.g. year or year+month).
M03.evidence:
M03. Date [ACQDATE]
Date on which you became the holder of the PGRFA. Date fragments are also accepted, e.g.
when only year or year and month are defined.

M04.name: Method
M04.descr: Event that occurred on the date in M03 which resulted in becoming the PGRFA holder; choose one of the enumerated options (e.g. Acquisition; In-house copy; In-house variant / Harvest-derived variant).
M04.evidence:
M04. Method1
Considering the date given for the previous field (Date), what event occurred on that date that
resulted in you becoming the PGRFA holder?
Choose one of the following:
1 Acquisition: you acquired the PGRFA from someone else. ...
2 In-house copy: you created the PGRFA by subsampling or taking a harvest from another
material that is under your management, with the intent that the new PGRFA should be, as
far as possible, a genetic copy of the parent. ...
3 In-house variant: you created the PGRFA by subsampling or taking a harvest from another
material that is under your management, where the parental sample is genetically variable
(such as a segregating population and/or physical mixture), and the PGRFA you are
registering is a genetic subset of the variability present in the parent.

standards.notes: The source document is a comprehensive list of named descriptors (many beyond M01–M04 are present in the full PDF). Here I have extracted the clearly visible core descriptors (M01–M04) with verbatim evidence quotes from the v2.1 document. If you want, I can extract the remaining descriptors (highly recommended and additional/context-dependent descriptors and their detailed allowable values) from the same source and include more precise data types (e.g. controlled vocabularies, ontology terms) where the document specifies them.
